## Medicine effects and recipes The Wasteland Medicine chapters list the current recipes and implemented effects. Field remedies and chemical mixtures may work differently; check the entry for the form you are making.
## Addiction Some performance chems can cause dependency. Repeated use can lead to withdrawal after the chem wears off. Follow the effects and cautions listed with each recipe.
## Mixing hazards Keep clean and dirty stimpak serum apart. Mixing them contaminates the clean serum. Mixing healing powder or healing poultice with stimpak or super stimpak serum creates black goo instead of a combined medicine.
## Chemical smoke A mask covering your face blocks inhalation of chemicals carried by smoke, even without an air tank. Pulling it down or taking it off leaves you exposed. A mask does not prevent chemicals from reacting with exposed skin.
## Fixer Fixer suppresses chem addiction effects. Its production recipe is in Performance chems. ## Hallucinations Chems that cause a high always produce one private encounter during that high: either imagined weather or one to three imagined enemies of the same kind (including molerats, ghouls, raiders, mutants, deathclaws and robots) rush you from near the edge of your view. Only you can see them or hear their voices. Enemies pass through walls. Each encounter has an equal chance of being harmless or damaging. Harmless enemies vanish when their apparent melee attack or shot reaches you and cause no damage. Damaging enemies repeatedly attack until you hit them or their temporary damage sends you critical. Their hits reduce your displayed health but cause no wounds or bleeding. At critical you briefly collapse, then their damage clears and you recover if your real injuries allow it. Clearing all enemies also removes their temporary damage. Real injuries are never healed. Both types disappear after twenty seconds at most. Give Up, Last Words and other critical-state actions are unavailable during the temporary hallucination collapse. One quarter of encounters instead show a random existing weather effect for twenty seconds, without an announcement. This weather is private and causes no radiation or temperature changes; the real weather is unchanged. Taking several chems during the same continuous high does not produce extra encounters.
Unstable is an optional Mental drawback that grants three trait points. Every five to twenty minutes, it has an eighty percent chance to cause one encounter even without a drug high. Failed rolls wait for the next interval. It does not add extra encounters during a high. While high or Unstable, hunger always makes imaginary cooked food appear nearby, and thirst always makes imaginary water or Nuka-Cola appear. Food and drink each have a separate ten-minute cooldown starting when they appear. They do not replace or delay enemy encounters. These private illusions vanish when you try to pick them up and provide no food or drink. Ordinary hunger and thirst alone do not cause them. Hallucinations highlight under your cursor and can be inspected with Shift-click like ordinary entities. Each new dose of a high-inducing chem has a five percent chance to cause Unstable for your current life. This acquired condition grants no trait points and is lost on respawn or a new round; it does not change your saved character.
